definitions.standard: The bouncing back of light rays when they hit a smooth or shiny surface.
definitions.simple: When light hits a mirror or a shiny object and bounces back into your eyes, like a bouncing ball.
definitions.scientific: The change in direction of a wavefront at an interface between two different media so that the wavefront returns into the medium from which it originated.

examples: Reflection of trees in a calm lake
counter_examples: Light getting absorbed by black paper (Absorption)

advanced_data.formula: Angle of Incidence (i) = Angle of Reflection (r)
advanced_data.history: The law of reflection was first accurately described by Euclid in 300 BC.

common_misconceptions: Only mirrors reflect light. (Fact: Everything that you can see, which doesn't produce its own light, is reflecting light.)
tutor_context.tutor_hint: Ask the student: 'If a red shirt doesn't glow like a lightbulb, how does its red color reach your eyes?'
